Nottingham Forest could now sign a player who could become as good as Adam Wharton

Lee Clarke
Sun 4 October 2026 19:06, UK Updated Mon 5 October 2026 9:24, UK
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:45
Instaread

Nottingham Forest could now look to sign a new player to replace Elliot Anderson in the January transfer window.

Forest added Xaver Schlager to the midfield ranks in the summer. With Oliver Glasner using James McAtee in the engine room too, Forest chose to go with what they had rather than going for a big-money option to replace Anderson.

Now, things could change, however. Kees Smit has been linked with Forest, and it would appear as though Glasner might have his eye on a player who could complement his squad just nicely.

You can choose ANY former Forest player to add to the current team, who are you picking and why? 👀

Like or Comment

Oliver Glasner told he can sign Adam Wharton type

Glasner will be learning more about his squad with each passing day. Forest won 2-1 against Swansea on Saturday, and that will have given the head coach a nice chance to look at some of his fringe players not away on international duty.

Now, it looks as though a midfielder could come into the squad during the January window. Forest have looked at Tyler Morton, and intriguingly, Glasner has been told he could be as good as Adam Wharton.

A Liverpool fan came to our TalkingPoints debate regarding the potential arrival of Morton, and he believes that the former Anfield gem could quickly become as good as Wharton, and that is exciting considering Glasner got the best out of the left-footed midfielder.

Lyon are once again in need of some finances. As a result, Morton is a wanted man ahead of the January transfer window and could be on his way back to the Premier League.

His former club Liverpool and Newcastle are both keen to land him when the window reopens. With that in mind, Forest may have to move very quickly to get this deal over the line once the window opens again.

The consensus has been that McAtee can be Glasner’s Wharton-type in the middle of the park. However, he’s still relatively new to the role, and perhaps Forest are keen to land a more natural player in the engine room.

Morton would represent a sound replacement for Anderson. His stock has risen significantly since he moved on from Liverpool, and at 23, he still has bags of unearthed potential that Forest could tap into.

Having a player who could emulate Wharton in his ranks would surely be ideal for Glasner. After five games, perhaps he’s seen enough when it comes to his midfield options, and it will be fascinating to see if Forest do press ahead for Morton.

The midfielders who could leave in January

If Forest were to sign Morton, surely it would signal the end for Nicolas Dominguez. He’s become a bit of a forgotten man this season at the City Ground, and he will surely want to play regular football.

There is also Ryan Yates, who has hardly played under Glasner either. He will likely want minutes, but losing him would pretty much signal the end of Forest’s long-standing run of having an academy graduate in every squad for over 80 years.

With Schlager, McAtee and Ibrahim Sangare as the first-choice options, Forest are rather stacked. With that in mind, Morton’s arrival would almost certainly signal a midfield departure, and it will be fascinating to see if the player does become Glasner’s Wharton-type once the window reopens.
